description:
New release workflow (release-v2.yml until dlv2-53 replaces release.yml) on push of tags v*. No tag-signature requirement (owner decision); safety comes from:
1. Tag creation restricted by ruleset v-tag-restricted; the tag must be annotated.
2. Admit the artifacts the trunk run already built and tested. Run `scripts/release_artifact_consumer.py admit` for the tag commit. It selects the latest exact-commit trunk.yml push run on develop, requires a successful dist-artifact job (trunk.yml:337-390), takes the attempt-bound dist artifact, and checks the recorded hashes. Then run `scripts/release_admitted_dist.py --stage` in the publishing job to confirm the directory is still the admitted one and stage the wheel and sdist. Publish only the staged bytes. Never rebuild.
3. T4: install+smoke on Python 3.11-3.14 x Linux/macOS/Windows (cross-OS correctness claims only after dlv2-defer-tpch-digest-darwin-arm64), UAT release-gate configs (tests/uat/configs/release-gate-*.yaml), _binaries hash manifest, make release-check (dlv2-50), ruleset drift (D7), no open release-blocking t3:* issue.
4. Build provenance attestation; publish via environment test-pypi or pypi (pypi keeps required reviewers: the owner approves real releases); GitHub release.
Legacy release.yml keeps working until dlv2-53 (G7).

Operating constraints (from docs/operations/release-artifacts.md and the trunk.yml artifact settings):
- Tag soon after the trunk run on the release commit finishes. The dist artifact expires after 90 days (trunk.yml:390).
- A rerun of the trunk run is a new attempt with its own artifact. The workflow admits the latest attempt only.
- Never fall back to an older run when the latest exact-commit run is missing, failed or expired. Refuse instead.
